proposition: According to Melvin-Koushki, Ibn Turka's modern reputation in Iran rests almost exclusively on the Tamhid al-Qawaʿid, taught in Imami seminaries; the Tamhid became a staple text 'probably' in the late Qajar period, and by the late 13th/19th century he was identified almost exclusively with it.

mediation.who: Āshtiyānī; Javādī Āmulī; Imami seminary tradition
mediation.note: The position is this scholar's own; we have it only as summarised by Melvin-Koushki.
MK argues a rival reading (Ibn Turka as occult philosopher) and in places calls this reading an error; his summary may compress or foreshorten it.
